newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India cements,autos slump in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India cements,autos slump in thin trade.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) were marked lower across the board in thin trade as cement and auto stocks tumbled.

"Cements and auto stocks came under pressure. Cement is a major comment on the economy because if those companies are not doing well then it means that the infrastructure projects are not being completed," said a trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed down 2.87 points, or 4.84 percent, at 56.32 points, with the premium over the local market at 16.90 percent compared with Friday's 18.50 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index fell 39.07 points, or 1.35 percent to 2,851.43.
"There was not much selling through the day, but U.S. investors turned nasty, especially after Wall Street opened down 50 points," said a trader.
At 1430 GMT, the Capel index had been down 3.91 percent.

Poor earnings at Associated Cement, India's largest cement company, dragged the GDRs of Gujarat Ambuja down 63 cents to $6.50/$7.50, while among auto stocks, Bajaj lost $1.00 to $26.50/$27.50 and Telco 75 cents to $8.75/$9.75.
"People see India as being a cheap market, but nobody wants to buy, even at these levels, and everyone is trying to run a flat book," said a trader.

The Capel Korea GDR Index ended down 2.03 points, or 3.01 percent, at 65.32, a premium of 31.30 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index ended 1.35 points higher at a provisional 727.83.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index added 4.31 points, 4.64 percent, to 97.31, a premium of 4.23 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index gained 156.75 points or 2.30 percent to 6,982.81.
